task.title: Pin the streaming memory bound in gitstore with an allocation-ceiling test
task.description:
Deferred from PR #36 (WB-01KYT6XA289VV2QNGTXZG9S31H, "Bound full history validation time and peak memory growth").

The memory half of that task is implemented by the streaming read in internal/gitstore/history.go:180-250: the object batch is started once and each candidate's response is consumed inside the per-task delivery loop, so only one commit's objects are resident at a time. Nothing in the Go suite defends that property.

The two tests added alongside the streaming rewrite are TestReadTaskHistoriesStreamDeliversEachTaskContiguouslyOldestFirst (internal/gitstore/history_test.go:407) and TestReadTaskHistoriesStreamReturnsHandlerErrorsUnchangedAndReleasesItsBatch (internal/gitstore/history_test.go:467). Both assert delivery order and handler-error propagation, and a whole-corpus buffering implementation satisfies both. The reviewer verified this on a copy of the worktree: rewriting ReadTaskHistoriesStream to collect every candidate's [4]batchObject into a buffered slice before the delivery loop and then replay it - the exact regression this PR exists to prevent - left `go test ./internal/gitstore/... ./internal/historyvalidation/... ./internal/cli/...` fully green. Only an off-repo `workbook-bench --storage-resources` run notices, and that does not run in CI.

The technique to close this already exists one file over: TestWalkCommitChainSizesItsCycleGuardToTheChainNotTheGraph (internal/gitstore/history_test.go:506) uses runtime.MemStats to pin per-walk allocation. An equivalent per-commit allocation ceiling over a multi-task, multi-depth fixture would assert that total allocation during ReadTaskHistoriesStream scales with task count rather than with total commits.

Deferred because the acceptance criterion for PR #36 is met by the measured evidence in docs/performance (peak resident memory above the git cat-file floor falls from 58.8 MB to 5.7 MB at depth 20 and from 694.8 MB to 0.1 MB at depth 200), and no behavior is wrong today. This is regression insurance, not a fix.
